title: istio-cni writes its CNI config files with mode 0600

detection.reason: a file mode on the node; the DaemonSet that writes the file is the subject

quote: The default file permissions for CNI config files written by Istio have changed from 0644 to 0600.
remediation: No action for the runtime, which reads the file as root. Node-level tooling that reads `/etc/cni/net.d/*istio*` as a non-root group member needs `values.cni.env.CNI_CONF_GROUP_READ=true` on the istio-cni DaemonSet (0640).
verifyCommand: kubectl get ds -A -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select([.spec.template.spec.containers[].image] | any(test("(istio|istio-release|istio.io/release)/install-cni"))) | .metadata.namespace + "/" + .metadata.name + " CNI_CONF_GROUP_READ=" + ([.spec.template.spec.containers[].env[]? | select(.name == "CNI_CONF_GROUP_READ") | .value] | join(","))'  # an empty value means CNI config files become 0600 at 1.30

title: The CNI agent now honours `excludeNamespaces` — ambient-labelled pods in an excluded namespace are un-enrolled

detection.reason: the exclusion list lives inside the istio-cni ConfigMap; the projection keeps ConfigMap keys, not the list

quote: Now, the CNI Agent respects excluded namespaces, which means existing, enrolled pods in an excluded namespace will be un-enrolled, and new, ambient-labeled pods in an excluded namespace will not be enrolled.
remediation: Compare `cni.excludeNamespaces` (the `EXCLUDE_NAMESPACES` key of the istio-cni-config ConfigMap, comma-separated) against namespaces labelled `istio.io/dataplane-mode=ambient`: pods in the overlap leave the mesh at 1.30. Remove the namespace from the exclusion list if they should stay enrolled.
verifyCommand: kubectl get cm -A -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(.metadata.name | test("istio-cni")) | .metadata.namespace + "/" + .metadata.name + ": " + (.data | to_entries | map(select(.key | test("exclude"; "i"))) | map(.key + "=" + .value) | join(" "))'  # a namespace printed under EXCLUDE_NAMESPACES that is also labelled istio.io/dataplane-mode=ambient is un-enrolled at 1.30

title: For a hostname defined in several namespaces, sidecars now prefer the Kubernetes Service, then the oldest other definition — not the alphabetically first namespace

detection.reason: a duplicated hostname is a cross-object comparison; ServiceEntries are the visible population since a Kubernetes Service alone cannot duplicate itself

quote: Istio now prefers Kubernetes services and falls back to the oldest non-Kubernetes service by creation time. Previously, the first visible namespace alphabetically was chosen.
remediation: Find hostnames that exist both as a ServiceEntry and as a Service (or as ServiceEntries in several namespaces): traffic may switch to a different definition at 1.30. Deduplicate them, or set `PILOT_SIDECAR_PICK_BEST_SERVICE_NAMESPACE=false` on istiod / `compatibilityVersion` 1.28 to keep the old choice.
verifyCommand: kubectl get serviceentries.networking.istio.io -A -o json | jq -r '[.items[] | .spec.hosts[]? as $h | {h: $h, ns: .metadata.namespace}] | group_by(.h) | map(select(.[1] != null)) | .[] | .[0].h + ": " + ([.[] | .ns] | join(","))'  # a printed host is defined by ServiceEntries in more than one namespace and may resolve differently at 1.30

title: istiod's XDS debug endpoints on port 15010 now require authentication — `--plaintext` tooling stops working

detection.reason: which tools read the plaintext XDS port is not on the cluster; the istiod Deployment carrying the opt-out is the subject

quote: XDS debug endpoints (syncz, config_dump) on port 15010 now require authentication. This affects istioctl commands using --plaintext flag and custom tooling using plaintext XDS.
remediation: Drop `--plaintext` from istioctl invocations and move custom XDS clients to the authenticated port (15012) with a service account token; `ENABLE_DEBUG_ENDPOINT_AUTH=false` on istiod restores the old behaviour.
verifyCommand: kubectl get deploy -A -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select([.spec.template.spec.containers[].image] | any(test("(istio|istio-release|istio.io/release)/pilot"))) | (.metadata.namespace + "/" + .metadata.name) as $n | .spec.template.spec.containers[].env[]? | select(.name | test("^(ENABLE_DEBUG_ENDPOINT_AUTH)$")) | $n + ": " + .name + "=" + (.value // "(valueFrom)")'  # no printed line means plaintext XDS debug access is refused after upgrade

title: Gateway API listeners with `protocol: TLS` are now honoured without `PILOT_ENABLE_ALPHA_GATEWAY_API`

detection.reason: Gateway API objects are not collected

quote: Gateway listeners with `protocol: TLS` (used for TLS passthrough via `TLSRoute`) are now accepted without requiring `PILOT_ENABLE_ALPHA_GATEWAY_API=true`, since TLSRoute graduated to GA in Gateway API v1.5.0.
remediation: A Gateway that already declared a `protocol: TLS` listener while the alpha flag was off starts serving it (and any attached TLSRoute) at 1.30. Confirm those listeners are meant to be live; remove them if not.
verifyCommand: kubectl get gateways.gateway.networking.k8s.io -A -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(.spec.listeners[]? | .protocol == "TLS") | .metadata.namespace + "/" + .metadata.name'  # a printed Gateway has a TLS listener that becomes active at 1.30 without the alpha flag

title: istiod 1.30 ignores a TLSRoute CRD below Gateway API bundle v1.5.0 — TLS passthrough routes stop being programmed

detection.reason: the bundle version is an annotation VALUE on the CRD and rules compare keys, not values; the hint names the TLSRoute CRD and the command prints its bundle version

quote: Gateway listeners with `protocol: TLS` (used for TLS passthrough via `TLSRoute`) are now accepted without requiring `PILOT_ENABLE_ALPHA_GATEWAY_API=true`, since TLSRoute graduated to GA in Gateway API v1.5.0.
remediation: istiod 1.30 watches TLSRoute at `v1` and drops a `tlsroutes.gateway.networking.k8s.io` CRD whose `gateway.networking.k8s.io/bundle-version` annotation is below v1.5.0: no TLSRoute is read, the Gateway reports `attachedRoutes: 0` and passthrough traffic fails with no error in the route's status. The opposite gate holds before the upgrade: 1.27.9, 1.28.6 and 1.29.2 onwards ignore a TLSRoute CRD above bundle v1.4.0. Upgrade the TLSRoute CRD to bundle v1.5.x in the same change window as istiod and expect TLSRoutes to be unserved by whichever control plane does not match it while both run. From 1.30.1, `istioctl analyze` reports a stale CRD as IST0176.
verifyCommand: kubectl get crd tlsroutes.gateway.networking.k8s.io -o custom-columns='CRD:.metadata.name,BUNDLE:.metadata.annotations.gateway\.networking\.k8s\.io/bundle-version' --ignore-not-found  # below v1.5.0 is ignored by istiod 1.30; above v1.4.0 is ignored by 1.27.9 / 1.28.6 / 1.29.2 onwards

title: Conflicting ListenerSet listeners are now rejected

detection.reason: ListenerSet objects are not collected; the ListenerSet CRD istiod reads from 1.30 (listenersets.gateway.networking.k8s.io, v1) is the subject

quote: Conflicting listeners are now correctly rejected and ListenerSet status conditions report in compliance with Gateway API 1.5.
remediation: A ListenerSet listener that conflicts on hostname or protocol with another listener on the same port stops being programmed after the upgrade. Check each ListenerSet's status conditions and give conflicting listeners distinct hostnames or ports first.
verifyCommand: kubectl get listenersets.gateway.networking.k8s.io -A -o json | jq -r '.items[] | .metadata.namespace + "/" + .metadata.name + " " + ([.status.listeners[]? | .name + ":" + ([.conditions[]? | select(.type=="Conflicted" and .status=="True") | "CONFLICTED"] | join(","))] | join(" "))'

title: Non-default defaultServiceExportTo / defaultVirtualServiceExportTo lists are honoured

detection.reason: meshConfig is not collected; istiod is the subject

quote: additional namespaces in meshConfig.defaultServiceExportTo and meshConfig.defaultVirtualServiceExportTo were not being honored when the default included the current namespace as ".".
remediation: Before 1.30.3 a default list other than the plain ["*"] was not applied as written (one holding "." plus namespaces kept objects private; one naming only namespaces exported them nowhere). After it, Services and VirtualServices without their own exportTo become visible exactly to the listed namespaces, so proxies there receive their config and VirtualService routing for the first time. Check the defaults list only the namespaces you mean.
verifyCommand: kubectl get configmap -n istio-system -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(.data.mesh != null) | "== " + .metadata.name, .data.mesh' | grep -E -A4 '^== |default(Service|VirtualService)ExportTo'  # any list other than ["*"] changes visibility at the upgrade

title: Waypoints apply the mesh default HTTP retry policy to the services they serve

detection.reason: which routes already set retries is not collected; namespaces and Services using a waypoint are the population

quote: The mesh config's defaultHttpRetryPolicy will apply to local services attached to waypoints.
remediation: Requests through a waypoint start being retried by the mesh default policy, as sidecars already did. For services where a retry is unsafe, set retries explicitly on their VirtualService (attempts: 0) before the upgrade.
verifyCommand: kubectl get ns,svc -A -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(.metadata.labels["istio.io/use-waypoint"] != null) | .kind + " " + (.metadata.namespace // "-") + "/" + .metadata.name + " waypoint=" + .metadata.labels["istio.io/use-waypoint"]'

title: A gateway using an external SDS provider requests the credential name, not sds://<provider>, as the SDS resource

detection.reason: whether the SDS server serves the credential name is not on the cluster; Istio Gateways with an sds:// credentialName are the population

quote: use the credential name (after stripping the `sds://` prefix) as the SDS resource name instead of the provider name.
remediation: After the upgrade a gateway without a local credential socket asks the external SDS server for the credential name with sds:// stripped (and `<credential-name>-cacert` for MUTUAL). Gateways whose pods mount the credential socket keep requesting the full sds:// name. Make the SDS server serve the certificate under the new name before upgrading, or TLS on those servers stops.
verifyCommand: kubectl get gateways.networking.istio.io -A -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select([.spec.servers[]? | (.tls.credentialName // "") | startswith("sds://")] | any) | .metadata.namespace + "/" + .metadata.name + " " + ([.spec.servers[]? | (.tls.credentialName // "") | select(startswith("sds://"))] | join(" "))'  # the SDS server must serve each printed credential name (sds:// stripped), plus NAME-cacert for MUTUAL

title: Cross-network ingress traffic to a Service labelled istio.io/ingress-use-waypoint now goes through its waypoint

detection.reason: the network topology and the waypoint's policies are not compared; Services with the label are the population

quote: multi-network ambient now routes to the waypoint when the ingress on one network calls a service on a different network
remediation: Ingress calls that cross networks used to skip the waypoint; they now pass through it, so its L7 AuthorizationPolicies and routing apply and a caller they do not admit gets 403. Check the waypoint's policies admit those callers before upgrading.
verifyCommand: kubectl get svc -A -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(.metadata.labels["istio.io/ingress-use-waypoint"] != null) | .metadata.namespace + "/" + .metadata.name + " waypoint=" + (.metadata.labels["istio.io/use-waypoint"] // "(namespace)")'  # check each waypoint's AuthorizationPolicies admit the cross-network ingress callers

title: Ingress gateways stop bypassing the waypoint for multi-cluster services on another network

detection.reason: the network topology and the waypoint's policies are not compared; Services with the label are the population

quote: causing authorization policies to not be enforced.
remediation: Requests from an ingress gateway to remote workloads on a different network now go through the waypoint, so authorization policies there apply and can deny traffic that used to pass. Check those policies admit the ingress gateway before upgrading.
verifyCommand: kubectl get svc -A -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(.metadata.labels["istio.io/ingress-use-waypoint"] != null) | .metadata.namespace + "/" + .metadata.name + " waypoint=" + (.metadata.labels["istio.io/use-waypoint"] // "(namespace)")'  # check each waypoint's AuthorizationPolicies admit the cross-network ingress callers

title: A ServiceEntry with a CIDR address now takes effect for ambient pods — the whole entry, not only the range

detection.reason: ServiceEntry addresses are not collected; the NONE and STATIC resolution ServiceEntries (the ones a CIDR address is valid on) are the population. Ambient (ztunnel) only: a mesh without a ztunnel DaemonSet is not affected.

quote: add support for cidrs in ztunnel
remediation: Up to 1.29 istiod dropped a ServiceEntry from ambient entirely when any of its addresses was a multi-IP range (10.0.0.0/24), so ambient pods never saw it. From 1.30 the whole entry reaches ztunnel: its hosts resolve, its ports and istio.io/use-waypoint label apply, and traffic to the range is matched to it. Review those ServiceEntries before upgrading and remove any that were never meant to take effect for ambient workloads.
verifyCommand: kubectl get serviceentries.networking.istio.io -A -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select([.spec.addresses[]? | select(contains("/") and (endswith("/32") or endswith("/128") | not))] | any) | .metadata.namespace + "/" + .metadata.name + " addresses=" + (.spec.addresses | join(",")) + " hosts=" + (.spec.hosts | join(",")) + " waypoint=" + (.metadata.labels["istio.io/use-waypoint"] // "none")'  # each entry starts applying to ambient pods at 1.30
